findings.title: traceID removed from plugin request completed log entries
findings.body: The refactoring removes the addition of traceID to logParams in logRequest. Previously, the logger middleware included the tracing trace ID in the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, but this PR deletes that logic (along with the tracing import). As a result, plugin request logs will no longer contain traceID, reducing correlation between logs and traces. This change is not mentioned in the PR description and appears unintentional.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new logger without shared log state
findings.body: The newly added FromContext method on TestLogger returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instead of returning the receiver or a logger that shares the same Logs fields. Any code that obtains a contextual logger via FromContext and then logs will write to a separate TestLogger instance, causing the original TestLogger's Logs to remain empty. This will break existing tests (e.g., for LoggerMiddleware) that pass a TestLogger and assert on its recorded log messages after invoking middleware methods.

findings.title: Logger name still references deprecated 'instrumentation'
findings.body: The logger is created with log.New("plugin.instrumentation"). Since the middleware has been renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and the contextual logging moved to a separate middleware, this logger name is outdated and may cause confusion. Consider renaming it to something like "plugin.requests" or "plugin.client" to align with the new naming convention.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is not covered by any tests. Given that it is responsible for injecting contextual attributes into the request context that LoggerMiddleware relies on, a regression here could break logging or context propagation. At minimum, tests should verify that instrumentContext correctly adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname to the context for the relevant client methods.
